project: The Formula of Becoming - Week 1 Day 6 - Full Cast

julian.instructions: Speak only Julian's supplied words. He is warm, smooth, and publicly confident, with a musician's sense of timing. Keep him welcoming rather than smug or seductive. Do not add words.

malik.instructions: Speak only Malik's supplied words. He is precise, guarded, economical, and quietly warm when trust appears. Use a measured medium-low delivery and dry humor without adding words.

narrator.instructions: Speak only supplied narration in a warm, grounded, observant, quietly lyrical documentary delivery. Be clear, restrained, and unhurried. Quicken slightly for campus montage. Do not perform character dialogue or add words.

nia.instructions: Speak only Nia's supplied words. She is bright, expressive, curious, and playful, with a lively conversational pace. Slow slightly for human consequences. Do not add words.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Indigo Night transformed Hart Student Union into a festival of music, food, club tables, and first-year students trying out possible versions of themselves.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Nia moved through it like a spark in dry grass. She signed an interest card for the Association for Women in Mathematics, took a flyer from Math Circle, promised to visit campus radio, and nearly volunteered for a service event before Malik removed the pen from her hand.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: You cannot join the whole university tonight.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: Watch me.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: I am watching. It is concerning.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Across the terrace, an alto saxophone climbed above the crowd. A small group from the Marching Herons was performing beside the radio booth. The saxophonist played with his eyes half closed, then opened them at the exact moment Nia stepped closer.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: After the set, he introduced himself as Julian Cross, second-year media arts student, campus radio host, and, according to him,

utterances.speaker: julian
utterances.text: occasional rescuer of boring events.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: This event was not boring,

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Nia said.

utterances.speaker: julian
utterances.text: Then I can take the night off.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: His confidence should have been irritating. Somehow, it was not.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Julian told her about a radio showcase on Friday and invited her to stop by. Nia said yes with the speed she used for nearly every interesting opportunity.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: At another table, Malik found a sign for the Heron Analytics Challenge. Fourth-down decisions. Player performance. Ticket demand. Real datasets, competitive teams, regional presentations.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: He read every line twice before writing his name.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: When he and Nia met again near the Copper Cup Cafe, they both had news.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: I got invited to the radio showcase,

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Nia said.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: I signed up for an analytics information session.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: Look at us choosing things.

utterances.speaker: malik
utterances.text: You chose six things.

utterances.speaker: nia
utterances.text: Seven, technically.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: He shook his head, but his attention drifted to Julian across the room. Julian saw Nia and lifted two fingers in a casual salute. She smiled back.

utterances.speaker: narrator
utterances.text: Malik did not yet have a name for the small drop inside his chest. He treated it like a number too minor to enter.
